headline: Hackett Hill land to be looked at for public sale; 784 Corning Road purchase request stays tabled.
summary: Attorney Garth Corriveau asked the city to consider selling five Hackett Hill parcels to Tech Freedom Village LLC. Committee members questioned the team about ledge, granite, site work, and due diligence, which Corriveau estimated at two to four months. After a private session, the chairman said the city will look at a public sale of the property.
decisions: Decided to look at opening a public sale of the Hackett Hill property in the future.
Received and filed the communications on tax deed notices and the Hackett Hill purchase request.
Left the purchase request for land at 784 Corning Road on the table.

decision_evidence.quote: In our discussions, we decided that in full transparency and obviously doing what is best for the city, which is our role here, that we are going to look at opening up a public sale of this property in the future.
On motion of Alderman Kaw-uh, duly seconded by Alderman Bonilla, it was voted to receive and file.

3. Communication from Attorney Andrew Sullivan on behalf of his client, 784 Corning Road LLC, requesting to purchase land at 784 Corning Road via private sale. (Note: Tabled on March 17, 2026, on request of Attorney Sullivan.) This item remained on the table.

decision_titles: Possible public sale of Hackett Hill property
Tax deed and Hackett Hill communications
Private sale request for land at 784 Corning Road
transcript:
## COMMITTEE ON LANDS AND BUILDINGS

October 20, 2026 at 6:00 PM

Chairman Trisciani called the meeting to order.

The Clerk called the roll.

Present: Aldermen Trisciani, Sapienza, Bonilla, Kaw-uh, Kantor

Messrs.: B. Masewic Adams, G. Corriveau, Raechel Lambert, Ryan Lambert, B. Sachs

1. Communication from Brenda Masewic Adams, Tax Collector, regarding notices of tax deed execution.

B. Masewic Adams, Tax Collector: I just wanted to add, all the accounts have been paid in full. So the communication you received is a little bit behind. So all 2023 back taxes have been paid in full. We are not dealing any of those properties.

2. Communication from Attorney Garth Corriveau, on behalf of his client, Tech Freedom Village LLC, requesting to purchase five (5) city-owned parcels located at Hackett Hill.

Chairman Trisciani: I think given our timeline and that we have until 6:30 for our private session, we don't have time for a presentation. We all did receive it in our packet. We do have a few questions.

Alderman Kaw-uh: Do we have to go into non-public before we start this?

Chairman Trisciani: No; non-public will be after this. These are public questions.

Chairman Trisciani: Thank you for the materials and giving us a thorough overview. In all of the correspondence, I didn't see any offer of a purchase price. What is the offer that you're actually making?

Garth Corriveau, Devine Millimet Attorneys at Law: Essentially it is the committee's decision whether or not to engage in negotiations with us, to go out to an RFP, or to flat out reject the request.

Chairman Trisciani: So basically, you have no offer to make?

G. Corriveau: No, we do. But we need your authority to proceed with that.

Chairman Trisciani: Looking at the plan, we know that lot M is going to be largely subject to the ten year highway plan. And this is a very large development that we're talking about. Would you consider doing a deal on the F, G, H, and I lots, and then as we progress through your phasing, at that point look at lot M for purchase?

Benjamin Sachs, Reframe Systems: I think we could definitely look at that, potentially. We'll be phasing it in the first phase on the first four lots and then lot M afterwards. But we do think M is quite important just because it gives us the opportunity to kind of expand with that later phase and have a much bigger impact on the city and really build out the whole innovation district.

Alderman Sapienza: How do you plan on dealing with all of the obstacles that have thwarted all of the other plans before that have come? We've been down this road before, quite literally, I mean the ledge and everything else. I'm curious to know. I mean, you're obviously aware of all these problems, right? We've talked about Hackett Hill several times in the past. How are you going to deal with the X amount of problems?

Raechel Lambert, DNNR: I believe Jeremy Hitchcock would be best to answer those things, since he has built out a bunch of projects. He's not here. I'm so sorry he's not here, but we hope that because we're choosing Manchester, we hope Manchester will choose us. We're anticipating that the site work is going to be the biggest challenge of this project, not filling it with founders and tenants. We're aware that it's a challenge and that's why a lot of people have walked away from the project.

Alderman Sapienza: Do you have a plan for us for dealing with the ledge and the granite?

B. Sachs: Once we have a negotiation in progress with the city, then we'll be able to do more engineering. And there's a lot of surveys and geotechnical investigations that still need to be done. We do have a really strong team and some creative ideas on how to do foundations. But yes, site work is definitely a challenge on this site, but it's something we're more than willing and excited to take on.

Alderman Kaw-uh: My question is related to some of those difficulties. Presumably, if you were to enter into negotiations with the city, there would be some sort of due diligence that you would want to do, obviously. How long of a time period would you expect that to be, given how large of a site it is and given how many different technical considerations there are?

B. Sachs: I think we'd have to speak with Jeremy a bit about that.

G. Corriveau: It's an excellent question. And part of me would actually want to defer to the city solicitor in some ways, because I don't want to speak for the city's end of negotiating due diligence. But in all honesty, having worked on due diligence in several transactions, we're talking months. Whether that's 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, we're talking 2 to 4 months in due diligence, I would think, to be realistic.

Alderman Kaw-uh: It would be fair enough given everything that's involved. I guess my concern at that point is that if the city decided that this land were to be sold to a developer, we would want to make sure that it is eventually sold to folks who have great confidence in their ability to deliver on what we're signing up for. And so my next question is what type of portfolio or prior experience would you bring to the table that could help justify a project of this scale?

Raechel Lambert: We're partnering with Jeremy Hitchcock on the building side, and I believe this is his 15th real estate development in the area. Ben is a world class architect and currently working with Reframe Housing, which is a modular robotics affordable home builder. And then Ryan and I are tech startup community builder people. I have an email list of 150,000 tech people. Whenever I tweet or email about it, it's extremely well received. So we're not worried about filling it with tenants, both commercial and residential. I think we have a great team to put it together, especially since we're all New Hampshire residents, we all love and live in New Hampshire, and myself and Ryan are apartment renters, so we don't have a lot of building expertise. But that's where Jeremy Hitchcock and Ben come in.

G. Corriveau: And I was also going to say Alderman, because you asked a very good question, the city's certainly going to want to undertake its own due diligence. So you know, it's a two way street and we're certainly going to be very open and transparent with the city as much as we can. I think the exciting thing about this, and by the way, I should say Jeremy wishes he could be here. He wished to convey to the committee that if the committee has additional questions, he is more than happy to come back at your next meeting and answer additional questions because I know that's important. This team as well as Jeremy, and Jeremy is one of the more accomplished business leaders this city has had in quite some time, but what's exciting about this opportunity is that it really is what the city has been looking to achieve. When I was an alderman back when TV was black and white, Hackett Hill went out to bid and there was one bid and that was it, at a time when the market was terrible. It was not for a tech campus. It was not for an innovation district. You all came up with that, and that's always been the true purpose of Hackett Hill. And that's what I find exciting about this; maybe the city can finally realize that potential that we've been talking about for north of 20 years now.

Chairman Trisciani: We're running up against time, so I want to make sure questions get answered. Alderman Bonilla, you had a question.

Alderman Bonilla: Like I discussed last time to you, my thing is with a village like this, for me, it's very critical to have it also serve the community, serving our students, let's say MST. How do you fully anticipate integrating students from MST into villages like this? How will our community have access to the services and to community space? Our communities have to have access to this too, not just the residents that it will house. So when I think of STEM, I want our students here in our Manchester public schools to have a pipeline to careers that pay, to have an opportunity of purchasing a home here, to build up their family. So that's really important to me. I'm very interested in the current estimated values of the lot sizes that we have.

Ryan Lambert, DNNR: Whenever anybody talks about taking high schoolers and giving them a promising future or hiring them straight out of high school into a tech job, hell yeah. I want to do that. My dream for Freedom Village is that it's a place that - a lot of real estate developments use this word programming, and it usually just means a pool table. There's a pool table, and places where people can host activities. We're all going to live here and we love hosting events. We love hosting. You heard about Freedom Summit a while ago. We love hosting hackathons. They like to get kids on the field, so to speak, and get them in and playing. I would love to partner with everybody like the community college, the high schools, get them to come hang out at our media lab, come play with the 3D printers. The companies that are working there, they're going to want to hire people that are curious, especially in the age of AI, when my little cousins that grew up in New Hampshire they're actually thinking right now if they should even go to college. And usually the alternative is they are going to go into the trades. Frankly, a lot of companies now are thinking, I'm just going to hire straight out of high school. How are we going to do that? I'd love for Freedom Village to be that kind of place. Come over and hang out and build stuff.

On motion of Alderman Sapienza , duly seconded by Alderman Bonilla , it was voted unanimously on a roll call vote to enter into non-public session pursuant to RSA 91-A:3, II(d) for consideration of property acquisition, sale or lease of real or personal property which, if discussed in public, would likely benefit a party or parties whose interests are adverse to those of the general community.

Chairman Trisciani called the meeting back to order.

On motion of Alderman Sapienza , duly seconded by Alderman Bonilla , it was voted to seal the minutes of the non-public session so that the proposed actions and decisions reached in non-public session are not rendered ineffective.

Chairman Trisciani: In our discussions, we decided that in full transparency and obviously doing what is best for the city, which is our role here, that we are going to look at opening up a public sale of this property in the future.

On motion of Alderman Kaw-uh , duly seconded by Alderman Bonilla , it was voted to receive and file.

TABLED ITEM

3. Communication from Attorney Andrew Sullivan on behalf of his client, 784 Corning Road LLC, requesting to purchase land at 784 Corning Road via private sale.

(Note: Tabled on March 17, 2026, on request of Attorney Sullivan.)

This item remained on the table.

There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Sapienza , duly seconded by

Alderman Bonilla , it was voted to adjourn.

A True Record. Attest.

Clerk of Committee
